test_title: RRB Group D 2025 (New Pattern) Official Mock Test
subject: general
question: Which of the following Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) laboratories conducted long-duration Active Cooled Scramjet Subscale Combustor ground testing for over 1,000 seconds in April 2025?

options.text: Defence Research and Development Establishment (DRDE), Gwalior

solution:
The correct answer is __**Defence Research & Development Laboratory (DRDL), Hyderabad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Defence Research & Development Laboratory (DRDL)** is one of the key laboratories under the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** located in Hyderabad.
 
• In **April 2025**, DRDL successfully conducted a long-duration **Active Cooled Scramjet Subscale Combustor ground testing** for over **1,000 seconds**, which is a significant milestone in hypersonic propulsion technology.
 
• The **scramjet engine** is a type of air-breathing engine used for hypersonic vehicles, and the tests at DRDL were aimed at validating the combustor's performance under simulated conditions. *Hence, the correct answer is DRDL.*
 
• The **ground testing** involved the use of an active cooling system, which is essential for maintaining the integrity of the combustor materials and ensuring prolonged operation at high temperatures.
 
• This achievement demonstrates India's growing capabilities in the field of **hypersonic propulsion systems**, an area critical for the development of futuristic defense applications.
 
• While other DRDO labs such as NSTL, DRDE, and GTRE contribute to defense research, the development and testing of scramjet engines fall under the expertise of DRDL.
 
• DRDL's work aligns with India's ambitions to enhance its defense technology and achieve self-reliance in advanced aerospace systems. *Hence, DRDL is the correct laboratory associated with this achievement.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Defence Research & Development Organisation (DRDO):**

 
 
• DRDO is India's premier organization for defense and aerospace research, headquartered in **New Delhi**. It operates under the Ministry of Defence.
 
• The organization focuses on the development of cutting-edge technologies such as **missiles, radars, electronic warfare systems, and hypersonic technologies**.
 
 
 
• **Defence Research & Development Laboratory (DRDL):**
 
 
• DRDL is based in **Hyderabad** and specializes in research related to **missile systems and propulsion technologies**.
 
• It has been instrumental in the development of India's missile systems, including the **Agni, Prithvi, and Akash series**.
 
 
 
• **Scramjet Technology:**
 
 
• **Scramjet**, or Supersonic Combustion Ramjet, is an air-breathing engine designed to operate at hypersonic speeds (Mach 5 and above).
 
• The scramjet engine's ability to use atmospheric oxygen as an oxidizer eliminates the need to carry heavy oxidizers, making it more efficient for **space exploration and defense systems**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Labs:**
 
 
• **NSTL, Visakhapatnam:** Focuses on naval systems and underwater weapons such as torpedoes and mines.
 
• **DRDE, Gwalior:** Engages in research related to defense against chemical and biological threats.
 
• **GTRE, Bangalore:** Specializes in gas turbine engines, primarily for aerospace applications.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Hypersonic Technology:**

 
 
• Hypersonic vehicles are capable of traveling at speeds greater than **Mach 5** and are critical for national defense and space exploration.
 
• The development of scramjet engines is a step toward achieving self-reliance in advanced aerospace systems.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Countries such as the **United States, China, and Russia** are also actively working on hypersonic technologies for defense and space applications.
 
• India's success in this domain enhances its position as a global leader in defense technology.
